name: cdsclient
desc: Tools for querying CDS databases for astronomical data
why: Queries CDS astronomical catalogues from the terminal, a real door into professional astronomy data.

brief.what_it_is: cdsclient is a package of C and shell programs for Unix and Linux that query astronomical databases hosted at CDS (Strasbourg) or its mirrors over the network. You give it sky positions or catalogue names and it returns matching rows in formats such as ASCII, HTML, TSV, XML, VOTable or FITS. Its generic tools are vizquery, which queries VizieR over HTTP, and find_cats, which batch-matches a list of positions against large surveys. The package also has many per-survey commands, such as findgsc, findpmm, find2mass and findwise, plus tools for finding catalogues and looking up bibcodes in SIMBAD.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says specific programs are faster than the generic vizquery because they connect straight to very large surveys (107 or more rows) instead of making general database queries. Its own description is 'a set of C and shell routines which can be built on Unix stations or PCs running Linux, which once compiled allow to query some databases located at CDS or on mirrors over the network.'
brief.how_it_works: Each program is a client that talks to a CDS server, mainly over port 1660, with vizquery using HTTP on port 80. A position list is supplied on stdin or as a file, and the program returns the matches within a radius, for example 5 arcminutes. The README says the CDSCLIENT environment variable can switch to port 80 or to an alternative server when port 1660 is blocked.

commands_seen.context: Configures the package for your system from the unpacked cdsclient-V.vv directory.
Configures installation into a prefix such as your home directory, so no root privilege is needed; executables go to ~/bin.
Installs executables, libraries and manpages to the configured prefix (default /usr/local).
Lists the basic options for a query program; the README says most programs support -help.
Finds GSC stars within 5 arcminutes of each centre listed in the file mycenters, read from stdin.
Finds USNO-A2.0 stars within 3 arcminutes of each centre in mycenters, sorted by distance from each centre.
Batch-queries the positions in my_file against GSC1.2, UCAC2 and 2MASS, with per-catalogue radius and magnitude arguments; the README example is split across lines and is joined here.
Retrieves SIMBAD bibliographic references from 1990 onward matching the words white, dwarf and X-ray.
Displays the ReadMe description file for catalogue VIII/59.

brief.install_notes: Download cdsclient.tar.gz from http://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/ftp/pub/sw/cdsclient.tar.gz or ftp://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/pub/sw/, then unpack with tar xvfz (or gzip -cd piped to tar on older systems). Run ./configure, make and make install from the cdsclient-V.vv directory. No accounts or API keys are mentioned. Network access is needed: port 1660 by default, or port 80 via CDSCLIENT=http. Proxies are set with the standard http_proxy variable.
brief.standout: It is a command-line door into professional astronomy archives. Pipe a file of coordinates through findgsc or findpmm and get back survey matches, with no web forms or scripting against an API. The bibliography tools also link SIMBAD references into LaTeX.
brief.status: The homepage is a documentation page dated 'Version 30-Dec-2009', and its program list runs to about March 2015 (URAT1). I found no release or commit history on the page, so the project looks quiet or static rather than actively developed. Treat that as an inference from the page dates, not a confirmed maintenance status.
brief.caveats: The README says the package is for Unix stations or Linux PCs, and it does not mention macOS or Windows. Build needs a C toolchain and the usual configure and make steps. Many surveys are historical (UCAC1, USNO-A1, GSC 1.1, DENIS older versions), and the page does not say which are still served. Program names in the doc do not always match the executables list (for example findgps6 in the doc versus findugps6 in the list, and findlas9 versus findulas9). Querying depends on CDS servers being reachable, and the README lists fallback servers in case the main one is down. The README asks for batch center files of about 40 MB or less. No licence is stated on the page. The Homebrew formula has no caveats.
quotes: The cdsclient package is a set of C and shell routines which can be built on Unix stations or PCs running Linux, which once compiled allow to query some databases located at CDS or on mirrors over the network.
Specific programs like find2mass or finducac3 are connecting directly to one of the very large surveys available from CDS (a very large survey has 107 or more rows).
Using a specific program is faster than the generic vizquery program which has to locate and transport the data via data-base queries
